summary_paragraph: A woman with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass status post reversal complicated by post-bariatric hypoglycemia requiring gastrostomy tube feeds and recurrent abdominal pain was admitted with three days of sharp epigastric/left-sided pain localized around the G-tube site with associated fullness and intermittent nausea/vomiting, without fever, GI bleeding, or obstructive symptoms. Evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs, and no evidence of tube-site infection; conservative management was pursued with NPO initially, dextrose-containing IV fluids to prevent hypoglycemia while tube feeds were held, and continuation of acid suppression and mucosal protection (PPI, H2 blocker, sucralfate) with symptom-directed analgesia/antiemetics. As pain improved off tube feeds, dextrose IV was weaned while frequent glucose checks remained stable and asymptomatic; due to poor oral intake on calorie counts, dronabinol (Marinol) was started with marked improvement in appetite, allowing the patient to meet ~90% of caloric needs by mouth. She received dietary counseling for outpatient hypoglycemia management (small frequent low-glycemic meals, protein snacks, glucose monitoring and Dexcom use) and was discharged home ambulatory and hemodynamically stable with stable sugars, continued GI medications, and planned surgical and dietitian follow-up to reassess the gastrostomy tube with a longer-term goal of removal in several months if stability persists.
